speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. To begin understanding the cause of your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood in your stool or unintended weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Campylobacter or similar bacterial etiology given camping exposure) with symptoms highly suggestive of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) overlap or Post-Infectious IBS. The combination of urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation is classic for colitis. We need to confirm if the acute infection has led to chronic inflammation.
